title: Upgrading PyHyperBatch — PyHyperBatch 4.2.0 documentation
text: Upgrading PyHyperBatch# Upgrading from PyHyperBatch 4.1 to 4.2# In HyperBatch 4.2, the minimum supported version for PyArrow has been raised from 15.0.0 to 18.0.0 in PyHyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.2, DataFrame.__getattr__ on HyperBatch Connect Python Client no longer eagerly validate the column name. To restore the legacy behavior, set PYHYPERBATCH_VALIDATE_COLUMN_NAME_LEGACY environment variable to 1. In HyperBatch 4.2, columnar data exchange between PyHyperBatch and the JVM uses Apache Arrow by default. The configuration hyperbatch.sql.execution.arrow.pyhyperbatch.enabled now defaults to true. To restore the legacy (non-Arrow) row-based data exchange, set hyperbatch.sql.execution.arrow.pyhyperbatch.enabled to false. In HyperBatch 4.2, regular Python UDFs are Arrow-optimized by default. The configuration hyperbatch.sql.execution.pythonUDF.arrow.enabled now defaults to true. To restore the legacy behavior for Python UDF execution, set hyperbatch.sql.execution.pythonUDF.arrow.enabled to false. In HyperBatch 4.2, regular Python UDTFs are Arrow-optimized by default. The configuration hyperbatch.sql.execution.pythonUDTF.arrow.enabled now defaults to true. To restore the legacy behavior for Python UDTF execution, set hyperbatch.sql.execution.pythonUDTF.arrow.enabled to false. In HyperBatch 4.2, PyPy is no longer officially supported. Run PyHyperBatch on CPython instead. In HyperBatch 4.2, HyperBatchSession.createDataFrame from a NumPy ndarray requires PyArrow (instead of pandas) and converts the array directly to Arrow rather than through pandas. Install PyArrow; if you previously ran with Arrow disabled and relied on NumPy-dtype-based schema inference, review the inferred schema, as it now follows Arrow’s type mapping. In HyperBatch 4.2, when a pandas UDF receives a nullable integer column whose batch contains nulls, the column is delivered as a pandas nullable integer extension dtype (Int8/Int16/Int32/Int64) instead of float64. Update UDF code that assumed float64 input for nullable integer columns. In HyperBatch 4.2, DataFrame.drop and Series.drop in pandas API on HyperBatch raise a KeyError when any of the specified labels is missing, instead of only when all of them are missing, matching pandas. Make sure all labels exist before dropping, filter to existing labels, or pass errors="ignore". In HyperBatch 4.2, a Python Data Source whose returned Arrow data has column types that do not match its declared schema fails with DATA_SOURCE_RETURN_SCHEMA_MISMATCH (column count and name mismatches already raised this error in earlier versions). Make the data source return data whose types match its declared schema. In HyperBatch 4.2, a SimpleDataSourceStreamReader whose read() returns a non-empty batch without advancing the end offset past the start offset fails with SIMPLE_STREAM_READER_OFFSET_DID_NOT_ADVANCE, instead of reprocessing the same batch and growing the prefetch cache without bound. Ensure the returned end offset advances past the last record. Upgrading from PyHyperBatch 4.0 to 4.1# In HyperBatch 4.1, Python 3.9 support was dropped in PyHyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.1, the minimum supported version for PyArrow has been raised from 11.0.0 to 15.0.0 in PyHyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.1, the minimum supported version for Pandas has been raised from 2.0.0 to 2.2.0 in PyHyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.1, DataFrame.__getitem__ on HyperBatch Connect Python Client no longer eagerly validate the column name. To restore the legacy behavior, set PYHYPERBATCH_VALIDATE_COLUMN_NAME_LEGACY environment variable to 1. In HyperBatch 4.1, Arrow-optimized Python UDF supports UDT input / output instead of falling back to the regular UDF. To restore the legacy behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.execution.pythonUDF.arrow.legacy.fallbackOnUDT to true. In HyperBatch 4.1, unnecessary conversion to pandas instances is removed when hyperbatch.sql.execution.pythonUDF.arrow.enabled is enabled. As a result, the type coercion changes when the produced output has a schema different from the specified schema. To restore the previous behavior, enable hyperbatch.sql.legacy.execution.pythonUDF.pandas.conversion.enabled. In HyperBatch 4.1, unnecessary conversion to pandas instances is removed when hyperbatch.sql.execution.pythonUDTF.arrow.enabled is enabled. As a result, the type coercion changes when the produced output has a schema different from the specified schema. To restore the previous behavior, enable hyperbatch.sql.legacy.execution.pythonUDTF.pandas.conversion.enabled. In HyperBatch 4.1, the data type BinaryType is by default mapped consistently to Python bytes in PyHyperBatch. To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.execution.pyhyperbatch.binaryAsBytes to false. The behavior before HyperBatch 4.1.0 is illustrated in the following table: Case Python type for BinaryType Regular UDF and UDTF without Arrow optimization bytearray DataFrame APIs (both HyperBatch Classic and HyperBatch Connect) bytearray Data sources bytearray Arrow-optimized UDF and UDTF with unnecessary conversion to pandas instances bytes In HyperBatch 4.1, the hyperbatch.sql.execution.pandas.convertToArrowArraySafely configuration is enabled by default. When this setting is enabled, PyArrow raises errors for unsafe conversions such as integer overflows, floating point truncation, and loss of precision. This change affects the return data serialization of arrow-enabled UDFs/pandas_udfs, and the creation of PyHyperBatch DataFrames. To restore the previous behavior, set the configuration to false. In HyperBatch 4.1, pandas API on HyperBatch works under ANSI mode when compute.ansi_mode_support is set to True (default). The safeguard option compute.fail_on_ansi_mode remains available, but it only takes effect when compute.ansi_mode_support is False. Upgrading from PyHyperBatch 3.5 to 4.0# In HyperBatch 4.0, Python 3.8 support was dropped in PyHyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.0, the minimum supported version for Pandas has been raised from 1.0.5 to 2.0.0 in PyHyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.0, the minimum supported version for Numpy has been raised from 1.15 to 1.21 in PyHyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.0, the minimum supported version for PyArrow has been raised from 4.0.0 to 11.0.0 in PyHyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.0, Int64Index and Float64Index have been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch, Index should be used directly. In HyperBatch 4.0, DataFrame.iteritems has been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch, use DataFrame.items instead. In HyperBatch 4.0, Series.iteritems has been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch, use Series.items instead. In HyperBatch 4.0, DataFrame.append has been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch, use ps.concat instead. In HyperBatch 4.0, Series.append has been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch, use ps.concat instead. In HyperBatch 4.0, DataFrame.mad has been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.0, Series.mad has been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.0, na_sentinel parameter from Index.factorize and Series.factorize has been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch, use use_na_sentinel instead. In HyperBatch 4.0, inplace parameter from Categorical.add_categories, Categorical.remove_categories, Categorical.set_categories, Categorical.rename_categories, Categorical.reorder_categories, Categorical.as_ordered, Categorical.as_unordered have been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.0, inplace parameter from CategoricalIndex.add_categories, CategoricalIndex.remove_categories, CategoricalIndex.remove_unused_categories, CategoricalIndex.set_categories, CategoricalIndex.rename_categories, CategoricalIndex.reorder_categories, CategoricalIndex.as_ordered, CategoricalIndex.as_unordered have been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.0, closed parameter from ps.date_range has been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.0, include_start and include_end parameters from DataFrame.between_time have been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch, use inclusive instead. In HyperBatch 4.0, include_start and include_end parameters from Series.between_time have been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch, use inclusive instead. In HyperBatch 4.0, the various datetime attributes of DatetimeIndex (day, month, year etc.) are now int32 instead of int64 from pandas API on HyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.0, sort_columns parameter from DataFrame.plot and Series.plot has been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.0, the default value of regex parameter for Series.str.replace has been changed from True to False from pandas API on HyperBatch. Additionally, a single character pat with regex=True is now treated as a regular expression instead of a string literal. In HyperBatch 4.0, the resulting name from value_counts for all objects sets to 'count' (or 'proportion' if normalize=True was passed) from pandas API on HyperBatch, and the index will be named after the original object. In HyperBatch 4.0, squeeze parameter from ps.read_csv and ps.read_excel has been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.0, null_counts parameter from DataFrame.info has been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch, use show_counts instead. In HyperBatch 4.0, the result of MultiIndex.append does not keep the index names from pandas API on HyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.0, DataFrameGroupBy.agg with lists respecting as_index=False from pandas API on HyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.0, DataFrame.stack guarantees the order of existing columns instead of sorting them lexicographically from pandas API on HyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.0, True or False to inclusive parameter from Series.between has been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch, use both or neither instead respectively. In HyperBatch 4.0, Index.asi8 has been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch, use Index.astype instead. In HyperBatch 4.0, Index.is_type_compatible has been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch, use Index.isin instead. In HyperBatch 4.0, col_space parameter from DataFrame.to_latex and Series.to_latex has been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.0, DataFrame.to_hyperbatch_io has been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch, use DataFrame.hyperbatch.to_hyperbatch_io instead. In HyperBatch 4.0, Series.is_monotonic and Index.is_monotonic have been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch, use Series.is_monotonic_increasing or Index.is_monotonic_increasing instead respectively. In HyperBatch 4.0, DataFrame.get_dtype_counts has been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch, use DataFrame.dtypes.value_counts() instead. In HyperBatch 4.0, encoding parameter from DataFrame.to_excel and Series.to_excel have been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.0, verbose parameter from DataFrame.to_excel and Series.to_excel have been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.0, mangle_dupe_cols parameter from read_csv has been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.0, DataFrameGroupBy.backfill has been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch, use DataFrameGroupBy.bfill instead. In HyperBatch 4.0, DataFrameGroupBy.pad has been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch, use DataFrameGroupBy.ffill instead. In HyperBatch 4.0, Index.is_all_dates has been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.0, convert_float parameter from read_excel has been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.0, mangle_dupe_cols parameter from read_excel has been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.0, DataFrame.koalas has been removed from pandas API on HyperBatch, use DataFrame.pandas_on_hyperbatch instead. In HyperBatch 4.0, DataFrame.to_koalas has been removed from PyHyperBatch, use DataFrame.pandas_api instead. In HyperBatch 4.0, DataFrame.to_pandas_on_hyperbatch has been removed from PyHyperBatch, use DataFrame.pandas_api instead. In HyperBatch 4.0, DatatimeIndex.week and DatatimeIndex.weekofyear have been removed from Pandas API on HyperBatch, use DatetimeIndex.isocalendar().week instead. In HyperBatch 4.0, Series.dt.week and Series.dt.weekofyear have been removed from Pandas API on HyperBatch, use Series.dt.isocalendar().week instead. In HyperBatch 4.0, when applying astype to a decimal type object, the existing missing value is changed to True instead of False from Pandas API on HyperBatch. In HyperBatch 4.0, pyhyperbatch.testing.assertPandasOnHyperBatchEqual has been removed from Pandas API on HyperBatch, use pyhyperbatch.pandas.testing.assert_frame_equal instead. In HyperBatch 4.0, the aliases Y, M, H, T, S have been deprecated from Pandas API on HyperBatch, use YE, ME, h, min, s instead respectively. In HyperBatch 4.0, the schema of a map column is inferred by merging the schemas of all pairs in the map. To restore the previous behavior where the schema is only inferred from the first non-null pair, you can set hyperbatch.sql.pyhyperbatch.legacy.inferMapTypeFromFirstPair.enabled to true. In HyperBatch 4.0, compute.ops_on_diff_frames is on by default. To restore the previous behavior, set compute.ops_on_diff_frames to false. In HyperBatch 4.0, the data type YearMonthIntervalType in DataFrame.collect no longer returns the underlying integers. To restore the previous behavior, set PYHYPERBATCH_YM_INTERVAL_LEGACY environment variable to 1. In HyperBatch 4.0, items other than functions (e.g. DataFrame, Column, StructType) have been removed from the wildcard import from pyhyperbatch.sql.functions import *, you should import these items from proper modules (e.g. from pyhyperbatch.sql import DataFrame, Column, from pyhyperbatch.sql.types import StructType). In HyperBatch 4.0, pandas API on HyperBatch will raise an exception if the underlying HyperBatch is working with ANSI mode enabled that is enabled by default, as it will not work properly with ANSI mode. To make it work, you need to explicitly disable ANSI mode by setting hyperbatch.sql.ansi.enabled to false. Alternatively you can set a pandas-on-hyperbatch option compute.fail_on_ansi_mode to False to force it to work, although it can cause unexpected behavior. Upgrading from PyHyperBatch 3.3 to 3.4# In HyperBatch 3.4, the schema of an array column is inferred by merging the schemas of all elements in the array. To restore the previous behavior where the schema is only inferred from the first element, you can set hyperbatch.sql.pyhyperbatch.legacy.inferArrayTypeFromFirstElement.enabled to true. In HyperBatch 3.4, if Pandas on HyperBatch API Groupby.apply’s func parameter return type is not specified and compute.shortcut_limit is set to 0, the sampling rows will be set to 2 (ensure sampling rows always >= 2) to make sure infer schema is accurate. In HyperBatch 3.4, if Pandas on HyperBatch API Index.insert is out of bounds, will raise IndexError with index {} is out of bounds for axis 0 with size {} to follow pandas 1.4 behavior. In HyperBatch 3.4, the series name will be preserved in Pandas on HyperBatch API Series.mode to follow pandas 1.4 behavior. In HyperBatch 3.4, the Pandas on HyperBatch API Index.__setitem__ will first to check value type is Column type to avoid raising unexpected ValueError in is_list_like like Cannot convert column into bool: please use ‘&’ for ‘and’, ‘|’ for ‘or’, ‘~’ for ‘not’ when building DataFrame boolean expressions.. In HyperBatch 3.4, the Pandas on HyperBatch API astype('category') will also refresh categories.dtype according to original data dtype to follow pandas 1.4 behavior. In HyperBatch 3.4, the Pandas on HyperBatch API supports groupby positional indexing in GroupBy.head and GroupBy.tail to follow pandas 1.4. Negative arguments now work correctly and result in ranges relative to the end and start of each group, Previously, negative arguments returned empty frames. In HyperBatch 3.4, the infer schema process of groupby.apply in Pandas on HyperBatch, will first infer the pandas type to ensure the accuracy of the pandas dtype as much as possible. In HyperBatch 3.4, the Series.concat sort parameter will be respected to follow pandas 1.4 behaviors. In HyperBatch 3.4, the DataFrame.__setitem__ will make a copy and replace pre-existing arrays, which will NOT be over-written to follow pandas 1.4 behaviors. In HyperBatch 3.4, the HyperBatchSession.sql and the Pandas on HyperBatch API sql have got new parameter args which provides binding of named parameters to their SQL literals. In HyperBatch 3.4, Pandas API on HyperBatch follows for the pandas 2.0, and some APIs were deprecated or removed in HyperBatch 3.4 according to the changes made in pandas 2.0. Please refer to the [release notes of pandas](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/dev/whatsnew/) for more details. In HyperBatch 3.4, the custom monkey-patch of collections.namedtuple was removed, and cloudpickle was used by default. To restore the previous behavior for any relevant pickling issue of collections.namedtuple, set PYHYPERBATCH_ENABLE_NAMEDTUPLE_PATCH environment variable to 1. Upgrading from PyHyperBatch 3.2 to 3.3# In HyperBatch 3.3, the pyhyperbatch.pandas.sql method follows [the standard Python string formatter](https://docs.python.org/3/library/string.html#format-string-syntax). To restore the previous behavior, set PYHYPERBATCH_PANDAS_SQL_LEGACY environment variable to 1. In HyperBatch 3.3, the drop method of pandas API on HyperBatch DataFrame supports dropping rows by index, and sets dropping by index instead of column by default. In HyperBatch 3.3, PyHyperBatch upgrades Pandas version, the new minimum required version changes from 0.23.2 to 1.0.5. In HyperBatch 3.3, the repr return values of SQL DataTypes have been changed to yield an object with the same value when passed to eval. Upgrading from PyHyperBatch 3.1 to 3.2# In HyperBatch 3.2, the PyHyperBatch methods from sql, ml, hyperbatch_on_pandas modules raise the TypeError instead of ValueError when are applied to a param of inappropriate type. In HyperBatch 3.2, the traceback from Python UDFs, pandas UDFs and pandas function APIs are simplified by default without the traceback from the internal Python workers. In HyperBatch 3.1 or earlier, the traceback from Python workers was printed out. To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.2, you can set hyperbatch.sql.execution.pyhyperbatch.udf.simplifiedTraceback.enabled to false. In HyperBatch 3.2, pinned thread mode is enabled by default to map each Python thread to the corresponding JVM thread. Previously, one JVM thread could be reused for multiple Python threads, which resulted in one JVM thread local being shared to multiple Python threads. Also, note that now pyhyperbatch.InheritableThread or pyhyperbatch.inheritable_thread_target is recommended to use together for a Python thread to properly inherit the inheritable attributes such as local properties in a JVM thread, and to avoid a potential resource leak issue. To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.2, you can set PYHYPERBATCH_PIN_THREAD environment variable to false. Upgrading from PyHyperBatch 2.4 to 3.0# In HyperBatch 3.0, PyHyperBatch requires a pandas version of 0.23.2 or higher to use pandas related functionality, such as toPandas, createDataFrame from pandas DataFrame, and so on. In HyperBatch 3.0, PyHyperBatch requires a PyArrow version of 0.12.1 or higher to use PyArrow related functionality, such as pandas_udf, toPandas and createDataFrame with “hyperbatch.sql.execution.arrow.enabled=true”, etc. In PyHyperBatch, when creating a HyperBatchSession with HyperBatchSession.builder.getOrCreate(), if there is an existing HyperBatchContext, the builder was trying to update the HyperBatchConf of the existing HyperBatchContext with configurations specified to the builder, but the HyperBatchContext is shared by all HyperBatchSession s, so we should not update them. In 3.0, the builder comes to not update the configurations. This is the same behavior as Java/Scala API in 2.3 and above. If you want to update them, you need to update them prior to creating a HyperBatchSession. In PyHyperBatch, when Arrow optimization is enabled, if Arrow version is higher than 0.11.0, Arrow can perform safe type conversion when converting pandas.Series to an Arrow array during serialization. Arrow raises errors when detecting unsafe type conversions like overflow. You enable it by setting hyperbatch.sql.execution.pandas.convertToArrowArraySafely to true. The default setting is false. PyHyperBatch behavior for Arrow versions is illustrated in the following table: PyArrow version Integer overflow Floating point truncation 0.11.0 and below Raise error Silently allows > 0.11.0, arrowSafeTypeConversion=false Silent overflow Silently allows > 0.11.0, arrowSafeTypeConversion=true Raise error Raise error In HyperBatch 3.0, createDataFrame(..., verifySchema=True) validates LongType as well in PyHyperBatch. Previously, LongType was not verified and resulted in None in case the value overflows. To restore this behavior, verifySchema can be set to False to disable the validation. As of HyperBatch 3.0, Row field names are no longer sorted alphabetically when constructing with named arguments for Python versions 3.6 and above, and the order of fields will match that as entered. To enable sorted fields by default, as in HyperBatch 2.4, set the environment variable PYHYPERBATCH_ROW_FIELD_SORTING_ENABLED to true for both executors and driver - this environment variable must be consistent on all executors and driver; otherwise, it may cause failures or incorrect answers. For Python versions less than 3.6, the field names will be sorted alphabetically as the only option. In HyperBatch 3.0, pyhyperbatch.ml.param.shared.Has* mixins do not provide any set*(self, value) setter methods anymore, use the respective self.set(self.*, value) instead. See HYPERBATCH-29093 for details. Upgrading from PyHyperBatch 2.3 to 2.4# In PyHyperBatch, when Arrow optimization is enabled, previously toPandas just failed when Arrow optimization is unable to be used whereas createDataFrame from Pandas DataFrame allowed the fallback to non-optimization. Now, both toPandas and createDataFrame from Pandas DataFrame allow the fallback by default, which can be switched off by hyperbatch.sql.execution.arrow.fallback.enabled. Upgrading from PyHyperBatch 2.3.0 to 2.3.1 and above# As of version 2.3.1 Arrow functionality, including pandas_udf and toPandas()/createDataFrame() with hyperbatch.sql.execution.arrow.enabled set to True, has been marked as experimental. These are still evolving and not currently recommended for use in production. Upgrading from PyHyperBatch 2.2 to 2.3# In PyHyperBatch, now we need Pandas 0.19.2 or upper if you want to use Pandas related functionalities, such as toPandas, createDataFrame from Pandas DataFrame, etc. In PyHyperBatch, the behavior of timestamp values for Pandas related functionalities was changed to respect session timezone. If you want to use the old behavior, you need to set a configuration hyperbatch.sql.execution.pandas.respectSessionTimeZone to False. See HYPERBATCH-22395 for details. In PyHyperBatch, na.fill() or fillna also accepts boolean and replaces nulls with booleans. In prior HyperBatch versions, PyHyperBatch just ignores it and returns the original Dataset/DataFrame. In PyHyperBatch, df.replace does not allow to omit value when to_replace is not a dictionary. Previously, value could be omitted in the other cases and had None by default, which is counterintuitive and error-prone. Upgrading from PyHyperBatch 1.4 to 1.5# Resolution of strings to columns in Python now supports using dots (.) to qualify the column or access nested values. For example df['table.column.nestedField']. However, this means that if your column name contains any dots you must now escape them using backticks (e.g., table.`column.with.dots`.nested). DataFrame.withColumn method in PyHyperBatch supports adding a new column or replacing existing columns of the same name. Upgrading from PyHyperBatch 1.0-1.2 to 1.3# When using DataTypes in Python you will need to construct them (i.e. StringType()) instead of referencing a singleton. On this page Show Source

title: Migration Guide: SQL, Datasets and DataFrame - HyperBatch 4.2.0 Documentation
text: HyperBatch SQL Guide Getting Started Data Sources Data Source V2 Performance Tuning Distributed SQL Engine PyHyperBatch Usage Guide for Pandas with Apache Arrow Migration Guide SQL Reference Error Conditions Migration Guide: SQL, Datasets and DataFrame Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 4.1 to 4.2 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 4.0 to 4.1 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 3.5 to 4.0 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 3.5.3 to 3.5.4 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 3.5.1 to 3.5.2 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 3.5.0 to 3.5.1 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 3.4 to 3.5 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 3.3 to 3.4 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 3.2 to 3.3 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 3.1 to 3.2 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 3.0 to 3.1 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 3.0.1 to 3.0.2 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 3.0 to 3.0.1 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 2.4 to 3.0 Dataset/DataFrame APIs DDL Statements UDFs and Built-in Functions Query Engine Data Sources Others Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 2.4.7 to 2.4.8 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 2.4.5 to 2.4.6 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 2.4.4 to 2.4.5 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 2.4.3 to 2.4.4 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 2.4 to 2.4.1 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 2.3 to 2.4 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 2.2 to 2.3 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 2.1 to 2.2 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 2.0 to 2.1 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 1.6 to 2.0 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 1.5 to 1.6 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 1.4 to 1.5 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 1.3 to 1.4 Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 1.0-1.2 to 1.3 Compatibility with Apache Hive Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 4.1 to 4.2 Since HyperBatch 4.2, HyperBatch enables order-independent checksums for shuffle outputs by default to detect data inconsistencies during indeterminate shuffle stage retries. If a checksum mismatch is detected, HyperBatch rolls back and re-executes all succeeding stages that depend on the shuffle output. If rolling back is not possible for some succeeding stages, the job will fail. To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.shuffle.orderIndependentChecksum.enabled and hyperbatch.sql.shuffle.orderIndependentChecksum.enableFullRetryOnMismatch to false. Since HyperBatch 4.2, support for Derby JDBC datasource is deprecated. Since HyperBatch 4.2, a new default method mergeWith has been added to the CustomTaskMetric interface. The default implementation sums the two metric values, which is correct for count-type metrics. Data source connector implementations that report non-additive metrics (e.g., maximum, average, compression ratio, or gauge values) must override mergeWith to provide correct merge semantics. Since HyperBatch 4.2, the virtual system catalog hosts the new system.builtin and system.session namespaces. system.builtin exposes built-in functions and functions injected through HyperBatchSessionExtensions; system.session exposes temporary views, temporary functions, and session variables created in the current session. As a result, 2-part references like builtin.func() and session.func() now follow a mini-path that tries the system namespace first and the current catalog second, so a persistent schema named builtin or session is no longer reached by builtin.func() / session.func() when the system namespace contains an object of the same name. To restore the previous behavior (current catalog first), set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.persistentCatalogFirst to true. Persistent schemas with these names are still allowed but should be reached with an explicit catalog prefix (for example, hyperbatch_catalog.session.x). See Reserved system names. Since HyperBatch 4.2, CREATE TEMPORARY VIEW, CREATE TEMPORARY FUNCTION, and the corresponding DROP statements accept the session and system.session qualifiers on the object name (in addition to the previously supported unqualified form); for example, CREATE TEMPORARY VIEW system.session.v AS ... and DROP TEMPORARY FUNCTION session.f are now valid. Any other qualifier on a temporary object is rejected with INVALID_TEMP_OBJ_QUALIFIER. Since HyperBatch 4.2, the SQL standard PATH feature is available: the SET PATH statement, the current_path() function, path-based resolution of unqualified routines, tables, views, and session variables, and the configurations hyperbatch.sql.path.enabled (default false) and hyperbatch.sql.defaultPath. The feature is opt-in; when hyperbatch.sql.path.enabled is false, unqualified resolution falls back to a fixed default path and SET PATH is rejected with UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE.SET_PATH_WHEN_DISABLED. See SET PATH and Name Resolution. Since HyperBatch 4.2, duplicate Common Table Expression (CTE) names within a single WITH clause are detected case-insensitively at parse time, so names that differ only in case (for example, WITH a AS (...), A AS (...)) are rejected with DUPLICATED_CTE_NAMES. This check is always case-insensitive and does not depend on hyperbatch.sql.caseSensitive. Rename the conflicting CTEs. Since HyperBatch 4.2, NATURAL JOIN honors the hyperbatch.sql.caseSensitive configuration when determining the common columns to join on. This can change which columns are used as join keys, and therefore the query result, when column names differ only in case. Since HyperBatch 4.2, when a SQL UDF has a parameter whose name matches a parameterless built-in function (current_user, current_date, current_time, current_timestamp, user, session_user, grouping__id), a bare reference to that name in the function body resolves to the built-in function instead of the parameter, matching the documented name resolution rules. Rename the parameter to avoid the collision, or set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.allowUdfParameterToShadowParameterlessFunction to true to restore the previous behavior. Since HyperBatch 4.2, SET CATALOG <name> resolves a bare (unquoted) name as a session variable first, using the variable’s value as the catalog name when such a variable exists, and otherwise treats the name as a literal catalog name. Use a string literal (SET CATALOG 'name') to force it to be interpreted literally. Since HyperBatch 4.2, when an error occurs while collecting observed metrics, Observation.get raises the underlying exception (for example, HyperBatchRuntimeException in Scala or PyHyperBatchException in Python) instead of silently returning an empty result. Add error handling if your code relied on receiving an empty result on failure. Since HyperBatch 4.2, GROUP BY GROUPING SETS (()) (and the equivalent empty GROUP BY CUBE() / GROUP BY ROLLUP()) is treated as a grand total and returns one row over empty input, matching an aggregation with no GROUP BY clause; previously it returned no rows. To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.analyzer.lowerEmptyGroupingSetToGlobalAggregate.enabled to false. Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 4.0 to 4.1 Since HyperBatch 4.1, the Parquet reader no longer assumes all struct values to be null, if all the requested fields are missing in the parquet file. The new default behavior is to read an additional struct field that is present in the file to determine nullness. To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.parquet.returnNullStructIfAllFieldsMissing to true. Since HyperBatch 4.1, the HyperBatch Thrift Server returns the corrected 1-based ORDINAL_POSITION in the result of GetColumns operation, instead of the wrongly 0-based. To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.hive.thriftServer.useZeroBasedColumnOrdinalPosition to true. Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 3.5 to 4.0 Since HyperBatch 4.0, hyperbatch.sql.ansi.enabled is on by default. To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.ansi.enabled to false or HYPERBATCH_ANSI_SQL_MODE to false. Since HyperBatch 4.0, CREATE TABLE syntax without USING and STORED AS will use the value of hyperbatch.sql.sources.default as the table provider instead of Hive. To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.createHiveTableByDefault to true or HYPERBATCH_SQL_LEGACY_CREATE_HIVE_TABLE to true. Since HyperBatch 4.0, the default behaviour when inserting elements in a map is changed to first normalize keys -0.0 to 0.0. The affected SQL functions are create_map, map_from_arrays, map_from_entries, and map_concat. To restore the previous behaviour, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.disableMapKeyNormalization to true. Since HyperBatch 4.0, the default value of hyperbatch.sql.maxSinglePartitionBytes is changed from Long.MaxValue to 128m. To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.maxSinglePartitionBytes to 9223372036854775807(Long.MaxValue). Since HyperBatch 4.0, any read of SQL tables takes into consideration the SQL configs hyperbatch.sql.files.ignoreCorruptFiles/hyperbatch.sql.files.ignoreMissingFiles instead of the core config hyperbatch.files.ignoreCorruptFiles/hyperbatch.files.ignoreMissingFiles. Since HyperBatch 4.0, when reading SQL tables hits org.apache.hadoop.security.AccessControlException and org.apache.hadoop.hdfs.BlockMissingException, the exception will be thrown and fail the task, even if hyperbatch.sql.files.ignoreCorruptFiles is set to true. Since HyperBatch 4.0, hyperbatch.sql.hive.metastore drops the support of Hive prior to 2.0.0 as they require JDK 8 that HyperBatch does not support anymore. Users should migrate to higher versions. Since HyperBatch 4.0, HyperBatch removes hive-llap-common dependency. To restore the previous behavior, add hive-llap-common jar to the class path. Since HyperBatch 4.0, hyperbatch.sql.parquet.compression.codec drops the support of codec name lz4raw, please use lz4_raw instead. Since HyperBatch 4.0, when overflowing during casting timestamp to byte/short/int under non-ansi mode, HyperBatch will return null instead a wrapping value. Since HyperBatch 4.0, the encode() and decode() functions support only the following charsets ‘US-ASCII’, ‘ISO-8859-1’, ‘UTF-8’, ‘UTF-16BE’, ‘UTF-16LE’, ‘UTF-16’, ‘UTF-32’. To restore the previous behavior when the function accepts charsets of the current JDK used by HyperBatch, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.javaCharsets to true. Since HyperBatch 4.0, the encode() and decode() functions raise MALFORMED_CHARACTER_CODING error when handling unmappable characters, while in HyperBatch 3.5 and earlier versions, these characters will be replaced with mojibakes. To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.codingErrorAction to true. For example, if you try to decode a string value tést / [116, -23, 115, 116] (encoded in latin1) with ‘UTF-8’, you get t�st. Since HyperBatch 4.0, the legacy datetime rebasing SQL configs with the prefix hyperbatch.sql.legacy are removed. To restore the previous behavior, use the following configs: hyperbatch.sql.parquet.int96RebaseModeInWrite instead of hyperbatch.sql.legacy.parquet.int96RebaseModeInWrite hyperbatch.sql.parquet.datetimeRebaseModeInWrite instead of hyperbatch.sql.legacy.parquet.datetimeRebaseModeInWrite hyperbatch.sql.parquet.int96RebaseModeInRead instead of hyperbatch.sql.legacy.parquet.int96RebaseModeInRead hyperbatch.sql.avro.datetimeRebaseModeInWrite instead of hyperbatch.sql.legacy.avro.datetimeRebaseModeInWrite hyperbatch.sql.avro.datetimeRebaseModeInRead instead of hyperbatch.sql.legacy.avro.datetimeRebaseModeInRead Since HyperBatch 4.0, the default value of hyperbatch.sql.orc.compression.codec is changed from snappy to zstd. To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.orc.compression.codec to snappy. Since HyperBatch 4.0, the SQL config hyperbatch.sql.legacy.allowZeroIndexInFormatString is deprecated. Consider to change strfmt of the format_string function to use 1-based indexes. The first argument must be referenced by 1$, the second by 2$, etc. Since HyperBatch 4.0, Postgres JDBC datasource will read JDBC read TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE as TimestampType regardless of the JDBC read option preferTimestampNTZ, while in 3.5 and previous, TimestampNTZType when preferTimestampNTZ=true. To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.postgres.datetimeMapping.enabled to true. Since HyperBatch 4.0, Postgres JDBC datasource will write TimestampType as TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, while in 3.5 and previous, it wrote as TIMESTAMP a.k.a. TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE. To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.postgres.datetimeMapping.enabled to true. Since HyperBatch 4.0, MySQL JDBC datasource will read TIMESTAMP as TimestampType regardless of the JDBC read option preferTimestampNTZ, while in 3.5 and previous, TimestampNTZType when preferTimestampNTZ=true. To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.mysql.timestampNTZMapping.enabled to true, MySQL DATETIME is not affected. Since HyperBatch 4.0, MySQL JDBC datasource will read SMALLINT as ShortType, while in HyperBatch 3.5 and previous, it was read as IntegerType. MEDIUMINT UNSIGNED is read as IntegerType, while in HyperBatch 3.5 and previous, it was read as LongType. To restore the previous behavior, you can cast the column to the old type. Since HyperBatch 4.0, MySQL JDBC datasource will read FLOAT as FloatType, while in HyperBatch 3.5 and previous, it was read as DoubleType. To restore the previous behavior, you can cast the column to the old type. Since HyperBatch 4.0, MySQL JDBC datasource will read BIT(n > 1) as BinaryType, while in HyperBatch 3.5 and previous, read as LongType. To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.mysql.bitArrayMapping.enabled to true. Since HyperBatch 4.0, MySQL JDBC datasource will write ShortType as SMALLINT, while in HyperBatch 3.5 and previous, write as INTEGER. To restore the previous behavior, you can replace the column with IntegerType whenever before writing. Since HyperBatch 4.0, MySQL JDBC datasource will write TimestampNTZType as MySQL DATETIME because they both represent TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE, while in 3.5 and previous, it wrote as MySQL TIMESTAMP. To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.mysql.timestampNTZMapping.enabled to true. Since HyperBatch 4.0, Oracle JDBC datasource will write TimestampType as TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE, while in HyperBatch 3.5 and previous, write as TIMESTAMP. To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.oracle.timestampMapping.enabled to true. Since HyperBatch 4.0, MsSQL Server JDBC datasource will read TINYINT as ShortType, while in HyperBatch 3.5 and previous, read as IntegerType. To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.mssqlserver.numericMapping.enabled to true. Since HyperBatch 4.0, MsSQL Server JDBC datasource will read DATETIMEOFFSET as TimestampType, while in HyperBatch 3.5 and previous, read as StringType. To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.mssqlserver.datetimeoffsetMapping.enabled to true. Since HyperBatch 4.0, DB2 JDBC datasource will read SMALLINT as ShortType, while in HyperBatch 3.5 and previous, it was read as IntegerType. To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.db2.numericMapping.enabled to true. Since HyperBatch 4.0, DB2 JDBC datasource will write BooleanType as BOOLEAN, while in HyperBatch 3.5 and previous, write as CHAR(1). To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.db2.booleanMapping.enabled to true. Since HyperBatch 4.0, The default value for hyperbatch.sql.legacy.ctePrecedencePolicy has been changed from EXCEPTION to CORRECTED. Instead of raising an error, inner CTE definitions take precedence over outer definitions. Since HyperBatch 4.0, The default value for hyperbatch.sql.legacy.timeParserPolicy has been changed from EXCEPTION to CORRECTED. Instead of raising an INCONSISTENT_BEHAVIOR_CROSS_VERSION error, CANNOT_PARSE_TIMESTAMP will be raised if ANSI mode is enable. NULL will be returned if ANSI mode is disabled. See Datetime Patterns for Formatting and Parsing. Since HyperBatch 4.0, A bug falsely allowing ! instead of NOT when ! is not a prefix operator has been fixed. Clauses such as expr ! IN (...), expr ! BETWEEN ..., or col ! NULL now raise syntax errors. To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.bangEqualsNot to true. Since HyperBatch 4.0, By default views tolerate column type changes in the query and compensate with casts. To restore the previous behavior, allowing up-casts only, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.viewSchemaCompensation to false. Since HyperBatch 4.0, Views allow control over how they react to underlying query changes. By default views tolerate column type changes in the query and compensate with casts. To disable this feature set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.viewSchemaBindingMode to false. This also removes the clause from DESCRIBE EXTENDED and SHOW CREATE TABLE. Since HyperBatch 4.0, The Storage-Partitioned Join feature flag hyperbatch.sql.sources.v2.bucketing.pushPartValues.enabled is set to true. To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.sources.v2.bucketing.pushPartValues.enabled to false. Since HyperBatch 4.0, the sentences function uses Locale(language) instead of Locale.US when language parameter is not NULL and country parameter is NULL. Since HyperBatch 4.0, reading from a file source table will correctly respect query options, e.g. delimiters. Previously, the first query plan was cached and subsequent option changes ignored. To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.readFileSourceTableCacheIgnoreOptions to true. Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 3.5.3 to 3.5.4 Since HyperBatch 3.5.4, when reading SQL tables hits org.apache.hadoop.security.AccessControlException and org.apache.hadoop.hdfs.BlockMissingException, the exception will be thrown and fail the task, even if hyperbatch.sql.files.ignoreCorruptFiles is set to true. Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 3.5.1 to 3.5.2 Since 3.5.2, MySQL JDBC datasource will read TINYINT UNSIGNED as ShortType, while in 3.5.1, it was wrongly read as ByteType. Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 3.5.0 to 3.5.1 Since HyperBatch 3.5.1, MySQL JDBC datasource will read TINYINT(n > 1) and TINYINT UNSIGNED as ByteType, while in HyperBatch 3.5.0 and below, they were read as IntegerType. To restore the previous behavior, you can cast the column to the old type. Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 3.4 to 3.5 Since HyperBatch 3.5, the JDBC options related to DS V2 pushdown are true by default. These options include: pushDownAggregate, pushDownLimit, pushDownOffset and pushDownTableSample. To restore the legacy behavior, please set them to false. e.g. set hyperbatch.sql.catalog.your_catalog_name.pushDownAggregate to false. Since HyperBatch 3.5, HyperBatch thrift server will interrupt task when canceling a running statement. To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.thriftServer.interruptOnCancel to false. Since HyperBatch 3.5, Row’s json and prettyJson methods are moved to ToJsonUtil. Since HyperBatch 3.5, the plan field is moved from AnalysisException to EnhancedAnalysisException. Since HyperBatch 3.5, hyperbatch.sql.optimizer.canChangeCachedPlanOutputPartitioning is enabled by default. To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.optimizer.canChangeCachedPlanOutputPartitioning to false. Since HyperBatch 3.5, the array_insert function is 1-based for negative indexes. It inserts new element at the end of input arrays for the index -1. To restore the previous behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.negativeIndexInArrayInsert to true. Since HyperBatch 3.5, the Avro will throw AnalysisException when reading Interval types as Date or Timestamp types, or reading Decimal types with lower precision. To restore the legacy behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.avro.allowIncompatibleSchema to true Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 3.3 to 3.4 Since HyperBatch 3.4, INSERT INTO commands with explicit column lists comprising fewer columns than the target table will automatically add the corresponding default values for the remaining columns (or NULL for any column lacking an explicitly-assigned default value). In HyperBatch 3.3 or earlier, these commands would have failed returning errors reporting that the number of provided columns does not match the number of columns in the target table. Note that disabling hyperbatch.sql.defaultColumn.useNullsForMissingDefaultValues will restore the previous behavior. Since HyperBatch 3.4, Number or Number(*) from Teradata will be treated as Decimal(38,18). In HyperBatch 3.3 or earlier, Number or Number(*) from Teradata will be treated as Decimal(38, 0), in which case the fractional part will be removed. Since HyperBatch 3.4, v1 database, table, permanent view and function identifier will include ‘hyperbatch_catalog’ as the catalog name if database is defined, e.g. a table identifier will be: hyperbatch_catalog.default.t. To restore the legacy behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.v1IdentifierNoCatalog to true. Since HyperBatch 3.4, when ANSI SQL mode(configuration hyperbatch.sql.ansi.enabled) is on, HyperBatch SQL always returns NULL result on getting a map value with a non-existing key. In HyperBatch 3.3 or earlier, there will be an error. Since HyperBatch 3.4, the SQL CLI hyperbatch-sql does not print the prefix Error in query: before the error message of AnalysisException. Since HyperBatch 3.4, split function ignores trailing empty strings when regex parameter is empty. Since HyperBatch 3.4, the to_binary function throws error for a malformed str input. Use try_to_binary to tolerate malformed input and return NULL instead. Valid Base64 string should include symbols from in base64 alphabet (A-Za-z0-9+/), optional padding (=), and optional whitespaces. Whitespaces are skipped in conversion except when they are preceded by padding symbol(s). If padding is present it should conclude the string and follow rules described in RFC 4648 § 4. Valid hexadecimal strings should include only allowed symbols (0-9A-Fa-f). Valid values for fmt are case-insensitive hex, base64, utf-8, utf8. Since HyperBatch 3.4, HyperBatch throws only PartitionsAlreadyExistException when it creates partitions but some of them exist already. In HyperBatch 3.3 or earlier, HyperBatch can throw either PartitionsAlreadyExistException or PartitionAlreadyExistsException. Since HyperBatch 3.4, HyperBatch will do validation for partition spec in ALTER PARTITION to follow the behavior of hyperbatch.sql.storeAssignmentPolicy which may cause an exception if type conversion fails, e.g. ALTER TABLE .. ADD PARTITION(p='a') if column p is int type. To restore the legacy behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.skipTypeValidationOnAlterPartition to true. Since HyperBatch 3.4, vectorized readers are enabled by default for the nested data types (array, map and struct). To restore the legacy behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.orc.enableNestedColumnVectorizedReader and hyperbatch.sql.parquet.enableNestedColumnVectorizedReader to false. Since HyperBatch 3.4, BinaryType is not supported in CSV datasource. In HyperBatch 3.3 or earlier, users can write binary columns in CSV datasource, but the output content in CSV files is Object.toString() which is meaningless; meanwhile, if users read CSV tables with binary columns, HyperBatch will throw an Unsupported type: binary exception. Since HyperBatch 3.4, bloom filter joins are enabled by default. To restore the legacy behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.optimizer.runtime.bloomFilter.enabled to false. Since HyperBatch 3.4, when schema inference on external Parquet files, INT64 timestamps with annotation isAdjustedToUTC=false will be inferred as TimestampNTZ type instead of Timestamp type. To restore the legacy behavior, set hyperbatch.sql.parquet.inferTimestampNTZ.enabled to false. Since HyperBatch 3.4, the behavior for CREATE TABLE AS SELECT ... is changed from OVERWRITE to APPEND when hyperbatch.sql.legacy.allowNonEmptyLocationInCTAS is set to true. Users are recommended to avoid CTAS with a non-empty table location. Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 3.2 to 3.3 Since HyperBatch 3.3, the histogram_numeric function in HyperBatch SQL returns an output type of an array of structs (x, y), where the type of the ‘x’ field in the return value is propagated from the input values consumed in the aggregate function. In HyperBatch 3.2 or earlier, ‘x’ always had double type. Optionally, use the configuration hyperbatch.sql.legacy.histogramNumericPropagateInputType since HyperBatch 3.3 to revert back to the previous behavior. Since HyperBatch 3.3, DayTimeIntervalType in HyperBatch SQL is mapped to Arrow’s Duration type in ArrowWriter and ArrowColumnVector developer APIs. Previously, DayTimeIntervalType was mapped to Arrow’s Interval type which does not match with the types of other languages HyperBatch SQL maps. For example, DayTimeIntervalType is mapped to java.time.Duration in Java. Since HyperBatch 3.3, the functions lpad and rpad have been overloaded to support byte sequences. When the first argument is a byte sequence, the optional padding pattern must also be a byte sequence and the result is a BINARY value. The default padding pattern in this case is the zero byte. To restore the legacy behavior of always returning string types, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.lpadRpadAlwaysReturnString to true. Since HyperBatch 3.3, HyperBatch turns a non-nullable schema into nullable for API DataFrameReader.schema(schema: StructType).json(jsonDataset: Dataset[String]) and DataFrameReader.schema(schema: StructType).csv(csvDataset: Dataset[String]) when the schema is specified by the user and contains non-nullable fields. To restore the legacy behavior of respecting the nullability, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.respectNullabilityInTextDatasetConversion to true. Since HyperBatch 3.3, when the date or timestamp pattern is not specified, HyperBatch converts an input string to a date/timestamp using the CAST expression approach. The changes affect CSV/JSON datasources and parsing of partition values. In HyperBatch 3.2 or earlier, when the date or timestamp pattern is not set, HyperBatch uses the default patterns: yyyy-MM-dd for dates and yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss for timestamps. After the changes, HyperBatch still recognizes the pattern together with Date patterns: [+-]yyyy* [+-]yyyy*-[m]m [+-]yyyy*-[m]m-[d]d [+-]yyyy*-[m]m-[d]d [+-]yyyy*-[m]m-[d]d * [+-]yyyy*-[m]m-[d]dT* Timestamp patterns: [+-]yyyy* [+-]yyyy*-[m]m [+-]yyyy*-[m]m-[d]d [+-]yyyy*-[m]m-[d]d [+-]yyyy*-[m]m-[d]d [h]h:[m]m:[s]s.[ms][ms][ms][us][us][us][zone_id] [+-]yyyy*-[m]m-[d]dT[h]h:[m]m:[s]s.[ms][ms][ms][us][us][us][zone_id] [h]h:[m]m:[s]s.[ms][ms][ms][us][us][us][zone_id] T[h]h:[m]m:[s]s.[ms][ms][ms][us][us][us][zone_id] Since HyperBatch 3.3, the strfmt in format_string(strfmt, obj, ...) and printf(strfmt, obj, ...) will no longer support to use 0$ to specify the first argument, the first argument should always reference by 1$ when use argument index to indicating the position of the argument in the argument list. Since HyperBatch 3.3, nulls are written as empty strings in CSV data source by default. In HyperBatch 3.2 or earlier, nulls were written as empty strings as quoted empty strings, "". To restore the previous behavior, set nullValue to "", or set the configuration hyperbatch.sql.legacy.nullValueWrittenAsQuotedEmptyStringCsv to true. Since HyperBatch 3.3, DESCRIBE FUNCTION fails if the function does not exist. In HyperBatch 3.2 or earlier, DESCRIBE FUNCTION can still run and print “Function: func_name not found”. Since HyperBatch 3.3, the table property external becomes reserved. Certain commands will fail if you specify the external property, such as CREATE TABLE ... TBLPROPERTIES and ALTER TABLE ... SET TBLPROPERTIES. In HyperBatch 3.2 and earlier, the table property external is silently ignored. You can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.notReserveProperties to true to restore the old behavior. Since HyperBatch 3.3, DROP FUNCTION fails if the function name matches one of the built-in functions’ name and is not qualified. In HyperBatch 3.2 or earlier, DROP FUNCTION can still drop a persistent function even if the name is not qualified and is the same as a built-in function’s name. Since HyperBatch 3.3, when reading values from a JSON attribute defined as FloatType or DoubleType, the strings "+Infinity", "+INF", and "-INF" are now parsed to the appropriate values, in addition to the already supported "Infinity" and "-Infinity" variations. This change was made to improve consistency with Jackson’s parsing of the unquoted versions of these values. Also, the allowNonNumericNumbers option is now respected so these strings will now be considered invalid if this option is disabled. Since HyperBatch 3.3, HyperBatch will try to use built-in data source writer instead of Hive serde in INSERT OVERWRITE DIRECTORY. This behavior is effective only if hyperbatch.sql.hive.convertMetastoreParquet or hyperbatch.sql.hive.convertMetastoreOrc is enabled respectively for Parquet and ORC formats. To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.3, you can set hyperbatch.sql.hive.convertMetastoreInsertDir to false. Since HyperBatch 3.3, the precision of the return type of round-like functions has been fixed. This may cause HyperBatch throw AnalysisException of the CANNOT_UP_CAST_DATATYPE error class when using views created by prior versions. In such cases, you need to recreate the views using ALTER VIEW AS or CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW AS with newer HyperBatch versions. Since HyperBatch 3.3, the unbase64 function throws error for a malformed str input. Use try_to_binary(<str>, 'base64') to tolerate malformed input and return NULL instead. In HyperBatch 3.2 and earlier, the unbase64 function returns a best-efforts result for a malformed str input. Since HyperBatch 3.3, when reading Parquet files that were not produced by HyperBatch, Parquet timestamp columns with annotation isAdjustedToUTC = false are inferred as TIMESTAMP_NTZ type during schema inference. In HyperBatch 3.2 and earlier, these columns are inferred as TIMESTAMP type. To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.3, you can set hyperbatch.sql.parquet.inferTimestampNTZ.enabled to false. Since HyperBatch 3.3.1 and 3.2.3, for SELECT ... GROUP BY a GROUPING SETS (b)-style SQL statements, grouping__id returns different values from HyperBatch 3.2.0, 3.2.1, 3.2.2, and 3.3.0. It computes based on user-given group-by expressions plus grouping set columns. To restore the behavior before 3.3.1 and 3.2.3, you can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.groupingIdWithAppendedUserGroupBy. For details, see HYPERBATCH-40218 and HYPERBATCH-40562. Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 3.1 to 3.2 Since HyperBatch 3.2, ADD FILE/JAR/ARCHIVE commands require each path to be enclosed by " or ' if the path contains whitespaces. Since HyperBatch 3.2, all the supported JDBC dialects use StringType for ROWID. In HyperBatch 3.1 or earlier, Oracle dialect uses StringType and the other dialects use LongType. Since HyperBatch 3.2, Parquet files with nanosecond precision for timestamp type (INT64 (TIMESTAMP(NANOS, true))) are not readable. To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.2, you can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.parquet.nanosAsLong to true. In HyperBatch 3.2, PostgreSQL JDBC dialect uses StringType for MONEY and MONEY[] is not supported due to the JDBC driver for PostgreSQL can’t handle those types properly. In HyperBatch 3.1 or earlier, DoubleType and ArrayType of DoubleType are used respectively. In HyperBatch 3.2, hyperbatch.sql.adaptive.enabled is enabled by default. To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.2, you can set hyperbatch.sql.adaptive.enabled to false. In HyperBatch 3.2, the following meta-characters are escaped in the show() action. In HyperBatch 3.1 or earlier, the following metacharacters are output as it is. \n (new line) \r (carriage ret) \t (horizontal tab) \f (form feed) \b (backspace) \u000B (vertical tab) \u0007 (bell) In HyperBatch 3.2, ALTER TABLE .. RENAME TO PARTITION throws PartitionAlreadyExistsException instead of AnalysisException for tables from Hive external when the target partition already exists. In HyperBatch 3.2, script transform default FIELD DELIMIT is \u0001 for no serde mode, serde property field.delim is \t for Hive serde mode when user specifies serde. In HyperBatch 3.1 or earlier, the default FIELD DELIMIT is \t, serde property field.delim is \u0001 for Hive serde mode when user specifies serde. In HyperBatch 3.2, the auto-generated Cast (such as those added by type coercion rules) will be stripped when generating column alias names. E.g., sql("SELECT floor(1)").columns will be FLOOR(1) instead of FLOOR(CAST(1 AS DOUBLE)). In HyperBatch 3.2, the output schema of SHOW TABLES becomes namespace: string, tableName: string, isTemporary: boolean. In HyperBatch 3.1 or earlier, the namespace field was named database for the builtin catalog, and there is no isTemporary field for v2 catalogs. To restore the old schema with the builtin catalog, you can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.keepCommandOutputSchema to true. In HyperBatch 3.2, the output schema of SHOW TABLE EXTENDED becomes namespace: string, tableName: string, isTemporary: boolean, information: string. In HyperBatch 3.1 or earlier, the namespace field was named database for the builtin catalog, and no change for the v2 catalogs. To restore the old schema with the builtin catalog, you can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.keepCommandOutputSchema to true. In HyperBatch 3.2, the output schema of SHOW TBLPROPERTIES becomes key: string, value: string whether you specify the table property key or not. In HyperBatch 3.1 and earlier, the output schema of SHOW TBLPROPERTIES is value: string when you specify the table property key. To restore the old schema with the builtin catalog, you can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.keepCommandOutputSchema to true. In HyperBatch 3.2, the output schema of DESCRIBE NAMESPACE becomes info_name: string, info_value: string. In HyperBatch 3.1 or earlier, the info_name field was named database_description_item and the info_value field was named database_description_value for the builtin catalog. To restore the old schema with the builtin catalog, you can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.keepCommandOutputSchema to true. In HyperBatch 3.2, table refreshing clears cached data of the table as well as of all its dependents such as views while keeping the dependents cached. The following commands perform table refreshing: ALTER TABLE .. ADD PARTITION ALTER TABLE .. RENAME PARTITION ALTER TABLE .. DROP PARTITION ALTER TABLE .. RECOVER PARTITIONS MSCK REPAIR TABLE LOAD DATA REFRESH TABLE TRUNCATE TABLE and the method hyperbatch.catalog.refreshTable In HyperBatch 3.1 and earlier, table refreshing leaves dependents uncached. In HyperBatch 3.2, the usage of count(tblName.*) is blocked to avoid producing ambiguous results. Because count(*) and count(tblName.*) will output differently if there is any null values. To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.2, you can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.allowStarWithSingleTableIdentifierInCount to true. In HyperBatch 3.2, we support typed literals in the partition spec of INSERT and ADD/DROP/RENAME PARTITION. For example, ADD PARTITION(dt = date'2020-01-01') adds a partition with date value 2020-01-01. In HyperBatch 3.1 and earlier, the partition value will be parsed as string value date '2020-01-01', which is an illegal date value, and we add a partition with null value at the end. In HyperBatch 3.2, DataFrameNaFunctions.replace() no longer uses exact string match for the input column names, to match the SQL syntax and support qualified column names. Input column name having a dot in the name (not nested) needs to be escaped with backtick `. Now, it throws AnalysisException if the column is not found in the data frame schema. It also throws IllegalArgumentException if the input column name is a nested column. In HyperBatch 3.1 and earlier, it used to ignore invalid input column name and nested column name. In HyperBatch 3.2, the dates subtraction expression such as date1 - date2 returns values of DayTimeIntervalType. In HyperBatch 3.1 and earlier, the returned type is CalendarIntervalType. To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.2, you can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.interval.enabled to true. In HyperBatch 3.2, the timestamps subtraction expression such as timestamp '2021-03-31 23:48:00' - timestamp '2021-01-01 00:00:00' returns values of DayTimeIntervalType. In HyperBatch 3.1 and earlier, the type of the same expression is CalendarIntervalType. To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.2, you can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.interval.enabled to true. In HyperBatch 3.2, CREATE TABLE .. LIKE .. command can not use reserved properties. You need their specific clauses to specify them, for example, CREATE TABLE test1 LIKE test LOCATION 'some path'. You can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.notReserveProperties to true to ignore the ParseException, in this case, these properties will be silently removed, for example: TBLPROPERTIES('owner'='yao') will have no effect. In HyperBatch version 3.1 and below, the reserved properties can be used in CREATE TABLE .. LIKE .. command but have no side effects, for example, TBLPROPERTIES('location'='/tmp') does not change the location of the table but only create a headless property just like 'a'='b'. In HyperBatch 3.2, TRANSFORM operator can’t support alias in inputs. In HyperBatch 3.1 and earlier, we can write script transform like SELECT TRANSFORM(a AS c1, b AS c2) USING 'cat' FROM TBL. In HyperBatch 3.2, TRANSFORM operator can support ArrayType/MapType/StructType without Hive SerDe, in this mode, we use StructsToJson to convert ArrayType/MapType/StructType column to STRING and use JsonToStructs to parse STRING to ArrayType/MapType/StructType. In HyperBatch 3.1, HyperBatch just support case ArrayType/MapType/StructType column as STRING but can’t support parse STRING to ArrayType/MapType/StructType output columns. In HyperBatch 3.2, the unit-to-unit interval literals like INTERVAL '1-1' YEAR TO MONTH and the unit list interval literals like INTERVAL '3' DAYS '1' HOUR are converted to ANSI interval types: YearMonthIntervalType or DayTimeIntervalType. In HyperBatch 3.1 and earlier, such interval literals are converted to CalendarIntervalType. To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.2, you can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.interval.enabled to true. In HyperBatch 3.2, the unit list interval literals can not mix year-month fields (YEAR and MONTH) and day-time fields (WEEK, DAY, …, MICROSECOND). For example, INTERVAL 1 month 1 hour is invalid in HyperBatch 3.2. In HyperBatch 3.1 and earlier, there is no such limitation and the literal returns value of CalendarIntervalType. To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.2, you can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.interval.enabled to true. In HyperBatch 3.2, HyperBatch supports DayTimeIntervalType and YearMonthIntervalType as inputs and outputs of TRANSFORM clause in Hive SERDE mode, the behavior is different between Hive SERDE mode and ROW FORMAT DELIMITED mode when these two types are used as inputs. In Hive SERDE mode, DayTimeIntervalType column is converted to HiveIntervalDayTime, its string format is [-]?d h:m:s.n, but in ROW FORMAT DELIMITED mode the format is INTERVAL '[-]?d h:m:s.n' DAY TO TIME. In Hive SERDE mode, YearMonthIntervalType column is converted to HiveIntervalYearMonth, its string format is [-]?y-m, but in ROW FORMAT DELIMITED mode the format is INTERVAL '[-]?y-m' YEAR TO MONTH. In HyperBatch 3.2, hash(0) == hash(-0) for floating point types. Previously, different values were generated. In HyperBatch 3.2, CREATE TABLE AS SELECT with non-empty LOCATION will throw AnalysisException. To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.2, you can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.allowNonEmptyLocationInCTAS to true. In HyperBatch 3.2, special datetime values such as epoch, today, yesterday, tomorrow, and now are supported in typed literals or in cast of foldable strings only, for instance, select timestamp'now' or select cast('today' as date). In HyperBatch 3.1 and 3.0, such special values are supported in any casts of strings to dates/timestamps. To keep these special values as dates/timestamps in HyperBatch 3.1 and 3.0, you should replace them manually, e.g. if (c in ('now', 'today'), current_date(), cast(c as date)). In HyperBatch 3.2, FloatType is mapped to FLOAT in MySQL. Prior to this, it used to be mapped to REAL, which is by default a synonym to DOUBLE PRECISION in MySQL. In HyperBatch 3.2, the query executions triggered by DataFrameWriter are always named command when being sent to QueryExecutionListener. In HyperBatch 3.1 and earlier, the name is one of save, insertInto, saveAsTable. In HyperBatch 3.2, Dataset.unionByName with allowMissingColumns set to true will add missing nested fields to the end of structs. In HyperBatch 3.1, nested struct fields are sorted alphabetically. In HyperBatch 3.2, create/alter view will fail if the input query output columns contain auto-generated alias. This is necessary to make sure the query output column names are stable across different hyperbatch versions. To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.2, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.allowAutoGeneratedAliasForView to true. In HyperBatch 3.2, date +/- interval with only day-time fields such as date '2011-11-11' + interval 12 hours returns timestamp. In HyperBatch 3.1 and earlier, the same expression returns date. To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.2, you can use cast to convert timestamp as date. Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 3.0 to 3.1 In HyperBatch 3.1, statistical aggregation function includes std, stddev, stddev_samp, variance, var_samp, skewness, kurtosis, covar_samp, corr will return NULL instead of Double.NaN when DivideByZero occurs during expression evaluation, for example, when stddev_samp applied on a single element set. In HyperBatch version 3.0 and earlier, it will return Double.NaN in such case. To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.1, you can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.statisticalAggregate to true. In HyperBatch 3.1, grouping_id() returns long values. In HyperBatch version 3.0 and earlier, this function returns int values. To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.1, you can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.integerGroupingId to true. In HyperBatch 3.1, SQL UI data adopts the formatted mode for the query plan explain results. To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.1, you can set hyperbatch.sql.ui.explainMode to extended. In HyperBatch 3.1, from_unixtime, unix_timestamp,to_unix_timestamp, to_timestamp and to_date will fail if the specified datetime pattern is invalid. In HyperBatch 3.0 or earlier, they result NULL. In HyperBatch 3.1, the Parquet, ORC, Avro and JSON datasources throw the exception org.apache.hyperbatch.sql.AnalysisException: Found duplicate column(s) in the data schema in read if they detect duplicate names in top-level columns as well in nested structures. The datasources take into account the SQL config hyperbatch.sql.caseSensitive while detecting column name duplicates. In HyperBatch 3.1, structs and maps are wrapped by the {} brackets in casting them to strings. For instance, the show() action and the CAST expression use such brackets. In HyperBatch 3.0 and earlier, the [] brackets are used for the same purpose. To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.1, you can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.castComplexTypesToString.enabled to true. In HyperBatch 3.1, NULL elements of structures, arrays and maps are converted to “null” in casting them to strings. In HyperBatch 3.0 or earlier, NULL elements are converted to empty strings. To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.1, you can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.castComplexTypesToString.enabled to true. In HyperBatch 3.1, when hyperbatch.sql.ansi.enabled is false, HyperBatch always returns null if the sum of decimal type column overflows. In HyperBatch 3.0 or earlier, in the case, the sum of decimal type column may return null or incorrect result, or even fails at runtime (depending on the actual query plan execution). In HyperBatch 3.1, path option cannot coexist when the following methods are called with path parameter(s): DataFrameReader.load(), DataFrameWriter.save(), DataStreamReader.load(), or DataStreamWriter.start(). In addition, paths option cannot coexist for DataFrameReader.load(). For example, hyperbatch.read.format("csv").option("path", "/tmp").load("/tmp2") or hyperbatch.read.option("path", "/tmp").csv("/tmp2") will throw org.apache.hyperbatch.sql.AnalysisException. In HyperBatch version 3.0 and below, path option is overwritten if one path parameter is passed to above methods; path option is added to the overall paths if multiple path parameters are passed to DataFrameReader.load(). To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.1, you can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.pathOptionBehavior.enabled to true. In HyperBatch 3.1, IllegalArgumentException is returned for the incomplete interval literals, e.g. INTERVAL '1', INTERVAL '1 DAY 2', which are invalid. In HyperBatch 3.0, these literals result in NULLs. In HyperBatch 3.1, we remove the built-in Hive 1.2. You need to migrate your custom SerDes to Hive 2.3. See HIVE-15167 for more details. In HyperBatch 3.1, loading and saving of timestamps from/to parquet files fails if the timestamps are before 1900-01-01 00:00:00Z, and loaded (saved) as the INT96 type. In HyperBatch 3.0, the actions don’t fail but might lead to shifting of the input timestamps due to rebasing from/to Julian to/from Proleptic Gregorian calendar. To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.1, you can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.parquet.int96RebaseModeInRead or/and hyperbatch.sql.legacy.parquet.int96RebaseModeInWrite to LEGACY. In HyperBatch 3.1, the schema_of_json and schema_of_csv functions return the schema in the SQL format in which field names are quoted. In HyperBatch 3.0, the function returns a catalog string without field quoting and in lower case. In HyperBatch 3.1, refreshing a table will trigger an uncache operation for all other caches that reference the table, even if the table itself is not cached. In HyperBatch 3.0 the operation will only be triggered if the table itself is cached. In HyperBatch 3.1, creating or altering a permanent view will capture runtime SQL configs and store them as view properties. These configs will be applied during the parsing and analysis phases of the view resolution. To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.1, you can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.useCurrentConfigsForView to true. In HyperBatch 3.1, the temporary view will have same behaviors with the permanent view, i.e. capture and store runtime SQL configs, SQL text, catalog and namespace. The captured view properties will be applied during the parsing and analysis phases of the view resolution. To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.1, you can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.storeAnalyzedPlanForView to true. In HyperBatch 3.1, temporary view created via CACHE TABLE ... AS SELECT will also have the same behavior with permanent view. In particular, when the temporary view is dropped, HyperBatch will invalidate all its cache dependents, as well as the cache for the temporary view itself. This is different from HyperBatch 3.0 and below, which only does the latter. To restore the previous behavior, you can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.storeAnalyzedPlanForView to true. Since HyperBatch 3.1, CHAR/CHARACTER and VARCHAR types are supported in the table schema. Table scan/insertion will respect the char/varchar semantic. If char/varchar is used in places other than table schema, an exception will be thrown (CAST is an exception that simply treats char/varchar as string like before). To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.1, which treats them as STRING types and ignores a length parameter, e.g. CHAR(4), you can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.charVarcharAsString to true. In HyperBatch 3.1, AnalysisException is replaced by its sub-classes that are thrown for tables from Hive external catalog in the following situations: ALTER TABLE .. ADD PARTITION throws PartitionsAlreadyExistException if new partition exists already ALTER TABLE .. DROP PARTITION throws NoSuchPartitionsException for not existing partitions Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 3.0.1 to 3.0.2 In HyperBatch 3.0.2, AnalysisException is replaced by its sub-classes that are thrown for tables from Hive external catalog in the following situations: ALTER TABLE .. ADD PARTITION throws PartitionsAlreadyExistException if new partition exists already ALTER TABLE .. DROP PARTITION throws NoSuchPartitionsException for not existing partitions In HyperBatch 3.0.2, PARTITION(col=null) is always parsed as a null literal in the partition spec. In HyperBatch 3.0.1 or earlier, it is parsed as a string literal of its text representation, e.g., string “null”, if the partition column is string type. To restore the legacy behavior, you can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.parseNullPartitionSpecAsStringLiteral as true. In HyperBatch 3.0.2, the output schema of SHOW DATABASES becomes namespace: string. In HyperBatch version 3.0.1 and earlier, the schema was databaseName: string. Since HyperBatch 3.0.2, you can restore the old schema by setting hyperbatch.sql.legacy.keepCommandOutputSchema to true. Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 3.0 to 3.0.1 In HyperBatch 3.0, JSON datasource and JSON function schema_of_json infer TimestampType from string values if they match to the pattern defined by the JSON option timestampFormat. Since version 3.0.1, the timestamp type inference is disabled by default. Set the JSON option inferTimestamp to true to enable such type inference. In HyperBatch 3.0, when casting string to integral types(tinyint, smallint, int and bigint), datetime types(date, timestamp and interval) and boolean type, the leading and trailing characters (<= ASCII 32) will be trimmed. For example, cast('\b1\b' as int) results 1. Since HyperBatch 3.0.1, only the leading and trailing whitespace ASCII characters will be trimmed. For example, cast('\t1\t' as int) results 1 but cast('\b1\b' as int) results NULL. Upgrading from HyperBatch SQL 2.4 to 3.0 Dataset/DataFrame APIs In HyperBatch 3.0, the Dataset and DataFrame API unionAll is no longer deprecated. It is an alias for union. In HyperBatch 2.4 and below, Dataset.groupByKey results to a grouped dataset with key attribute is wrongly named as “value”, if the key is non-struct type, for example, int, string, array, etc. This is counterintuitive and makes the schema of aggregation queries unexpected. For example, the schema of ds.groupByKey(...).count() is (value, count). Since HyperBatch 3.0, we name the grouping attribute to “key”. The old behavior is preserved under a newly added configuration hyperbatch.sql.legacy.dataset.nameNonStructGroupingKeyAsValue with a default value of false. In HyperBatch 3.0, the column metadata will always be propagated in the API Column.name and Column.as. In HyperBatch version 2.4 and earlier, the metadata of NamedExpression is set as the explicitMetadata for the new column at the time the API is called, it won’t change even if the underlying NamedExpression changes metadata. To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.0, you can use the API as(alias: String, metadata: Metadata) with explicit metadata. When turning a Dataset to another Dataset, HyperBatch will up cast the fields in the original Dataset to the type of corresponding fields in the target DataSet. In version 2.4 and earlier, this up cast is not very strict, e.g. Seq("str").toDS.as[Int] fails, but Seq("str").toDS.as[Boolean] works and throw NPE during execution. In HyperBatch 3.0, the up cast is stricter and turning String into something else is not allowed, i.e. Seq("str").toDS.as[Boolean] will fail during analysis. To restore the behavior before HyperBatch 3.0, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.doLooseUpcast to true. DDL Statements In HyperBatch 3.0, when inserting a value into a table column with a different data type, the type coercion is performed as per ANSI SQL standard. Certain unreasonable type conversions such as converting string to int and double to boolean are disallowed. A runtime exception is thrown if the value is out-of-range for the data type of the column. In HyperBatch version 2.4 and below, type conversions during table insertion are allowed as long as they are valid Cast. When inserting an out-of-range value to an integral field, the low-order bits of the value is inserted(the same as Java/Scala numeric type casting). For example, if 257 is inserted to a field of byte type, the result is 1. The behavior is controlled by the option hyperbatch.sql.storeAssignmentPolicy, with a default value as “ANSI”. Setting the option as “Legacy” restores the previous behavior. The ADD JAR command previously returned a result set with the single value 0. It now returns an empty result set. HyperBatch 2.4 and below: the SET command works without any warnings even if the specified key is for HyperBatchConf entries and it has no effect because the command does not update HyperBatchConf, but the behavior might confuse users. In 3.0, the command fails if a HyperBatchConf key is used. You can disable such a check by setting hyperbatch.sql.legacy.setCommandRejectsHyperBatchCoreConfs to false. Refreshing a cached table would trigger a table uncache operation and then a table cache (lazily) operation. In HyperBatch version 2.4 and below, the cache name and storage level are not preserved before the uncache operation. Therefore, the cache name and storage level could be changed unexpectedly. In HyperBatch 3.0, cache name and storage level are first preserved for cache recreation. It helps to maintain a consistent cache behavior upon table refreshing. In HyperBatch 3.0, the properties listing below become reserved; commands fail if you specify reserved properties in places like CREATE DATABASE ... WITH DBPROPERTIES and ALTER TABLE ... SET TBLPROPERTIES. You need their specific clauses to specify them, for example, CREATE DATABASE test COMMENT 'any comment' LOCATION 'some path'. You can set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.notReserveProperties to true to ignore the ParseException, in this case, these properties will be silently removed, for example: SET DBPROPERTIES('location'='/tmp') will have no effect. In HyperBatch version 2.4 and below, these properties are neither reserved nor have side effects, for example, SET DBPROPERTIES('location'='/tmp') do not change the location of the database but only create a headless property just like 'a'='b'. Property (case sensitive) Database Reserved Table Reserved Remarks provider no yes For tables, use the USING clause to specify it. Once set, it can’t be changed. location yes yes For databases and tables, use the LOCATION clause to specify it. owner yes yes For databases and tables, it is determined by the user who runs hyperbatch and create the table. In HyperBatch 3.0, you can use ADD FILE to add file directories as well. Earlier you could add only single files using this command. To restore the behavior of earlier versions, set hyperbatch.sql.legacy.addSingleFileInAddFile to true. In HyperBatch 3.0, SHOW TBLPROPERTIES throws AnalysisException if the table does not exist. In HyperBatch version 2.4 and below, this scenario caused NoSuchTableException. In HyperBatch 3.0, SHOW CREATE TABLE table_identifier always returns HyperBatch DDL, even when the given table is a Hive SerDe table. For generating Hive DDL, use SHOW CREATE TABLE table_identifier AS SERDE command instead. In HyperBatch 3.0, column of CHAR type is not allowed in non-Hive-Serde tables, and CREATE/ALTER TABLE commands will fail if CHAR type is detected. Please use STRING type instead. In HyperBatch version 2.4 and below, CHAR type is treated as STRING type and the length parameter is simply ignored.
